note: Every name carries a signed edge_score on -100..+100. There is no call and no threshold: rank on edge_score and cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what makes the ranking question answerable at every k.

findings.finding: July 2026 was the warmest month in the entire 131-year contiguous-US temperature record (76.9degF, all 48 states above their 20th-century average, none near or below normal) and it is the final and seasonally largest month of ServiceTitan's fiscal Q2, which ended 31 July 2026 - record cooling load is the direct driver of the emergency HVAC service calls and same-day replacement tickets that flow through Gross Transaction Volume and the payments take-rate, i.e. the ~25% of revenue that is variable ($66.8m of the $268.8m reported in Q1 was non-subscription).
findings.adversary_note: The underlying fact is not obscure by any measure: NOAA published the July 2026 CONUS record (76.9F, warmest month in the 1895-present record, all states in the warmest third) on 2026-08-10 and it was front-page national news the same day at NBC, CBS, PBS and Axios. Cooling-degree-day sensitivity is standard sell-side practice across the HVAC-adjacent complex, and the trade press ran the service-call consequence explicitly through June and July (ACHR News, 'Longer Heat Waves, Bigger HVAC Challenges'; local coverage of contractors running 6-7 calls per tech). ServiceTitan's fiscal calendar is public, so 'the record month is the last month of the quarter' is arithmetic anyone can do. What I could NOT find published is the specific transmission to the disclosed line item: no preview of tonight's print connects record cooling load to usage revenue or the payments take-rate on GTV. Every preview I found frames the quarter on Max/agentic AI, enterprise mix and operating margin. So there is a genuine residual, but it is a residual on a headline macro fact, and the arithmetic caps it hard. The weather-variable line is usage revenue, $58.5m of $268.8m in Q1 (21.8%, not 25% - professional services of $8.3m is implementation work and is not weather-driven, so the hunter's $66.8m non-subscription figure overstates the exposed base by about a seventh). Against a Q2 guide of $284-286m, only the July slice of usage (~$23m) was unknown when guidance was set on 2026-06-04; a 5-10% weather uplift on that slice is $1.1-2.3m, or 0.4-0.8% of revenue, on a name that already beat by 4.7% in Q1. Real, but a small share of a 10.08% implied move.

findings.finding: ServiceTitan bills roughly $245-400 per technician per month, so its subscription line is mechanically a function of how many technicians its contractors employ - and BLS JOLTS shows construction hires in July 2026, the last month of ServiceTitan's fiscal Q2, at 366,000, up 14.7% month-over-month and 9.9% year-over-year, the highest construction hiring rate in about two years, with openings at 326,000 (+9.4% m/m).
findings.adversary_note: This is a headline BLS release from 2026-09-02, six days before the print, carried by Construction Dive, ENR, Yahoo Finance and NAHB's Eye on Housing. There is no version of JOLTS that is obscure. But the more damaging point is that the transmission is largely broken, and the sources that published it say so themselves. First, the composition: ENR and Construction Dive both attribute the July strength to data-center and power construction, with data-center construction up 46% year over year. JOLTS 'construction' is the whole supersector - heavy and civil, nonresidential building, and specialty trade - and ServiceTitan sells to residential and commercial *service* contractors in HVAC, plumbing, electrical and roofing. A data-center construction hiring boom adds close to zero ServiceTitan seats. Second, hires is a gross monthly flow, not a headcount stock; the finding gives no separations figure, so a 14.7% m/m jump in hires is consistent with elevated churn and a flat technician base, which is what a seat-billed subscription line actually tracks. Third, timing: July is the last month of the quarter, so even a real seat gain contributes at most one month, against contracted subscription terms that were largely booked earlier. Subscription revenue was $202.0m in Q1; a 1% one-month seat lift is about $0.7m, roughly 0.25% of revenue. Fourth, net dollar retention above 110% already embeds seat expansion in the guide. And fifth, the interaction that matters: the market's live worry about this name is that the $245-400 per-technician-per-month seat model is what AI agents disrupt. A JOLTS print showing more technicians does not answer the question the multiple is being cut on.

findings.finding: The visible HVAC datapoint an analyst would cross-read into ServiceTitan is Lennox's 30-July print - residential revenue -7%, unit volume -12%, full-year growth guide cut from ~4% to ~1% - but that is a company-specific channel and share story (Lennox's own one-step volumes fell mid-teens, new construction -30%), while the industry-wide series over the same window went the other way: Watsco, the largest US HVAC distributor, reported domestic residential HVAC equipment sales +5% with unit volume +2% and ASPs +2% and titled its release 'further industry stabilization'; Lennox's own CEO said the repair-versus-replace trend 'has stabilized', and a repair-skewed market with record heat maximises job count and technician demand, which is what ServiceTitan monetises rather than equipment units.
findings.adversary_note: Both legs of this comparison are wire copy from the same day. Watsco's release is dated 2026-07-29 (globenewswire path /2026/07/29/, matching the EDGAR exhibit the hunter cites) and the '+5% domestic residential HVAC equipment, +2% units, +2% ASP' line is in the release body under a headline that literally reads 'Further Industry Stabilization'. It was picked up by Modern Distribution Management, ACHR News, HVACR Trends and Yahoo Finance within a day. Lennox reported the same morning, 2026-07-29 - the finding says '30-July', which is one day off - with Home Comfort Solutions revenue -7% to $936m on -12% units, and the divergence-versus-commercial framing was itself published (Investing.com, 'Lennox Q2 2026 slides: commercial strength offsets residential slump'). So neither the datapoint nor the contrast is unpublished; the word the market has been given for the residential end market since 29 July is Watsco's own word, 'stabilizing'. I also checked the AHRI series the brief warned me about, and the hunter is right to have discarded the stale 2025 figures: the current data is June 2026 shipments of 1,023,571 units, +21.7% y/y, with first-half 2026 +3.0% - published in trade press in August 2026 and supportive of the claim, though June 2025 was a depressed A2L-transition comp so the +3.0% half-year figure is the honest one. Two things keep this from being a 90. Watsco's quarter ends 30 June, so it covers only two of ServiceTitan's three months and misses the record July entirely. And the market's read of the Watsco print was negative - shares sank 15% on gross margin down 180bp - so the bullish residential-volume line inside a release the tape sold is arguably underweighted by consensus. That is a real but second-order point, and it is a defence against a bear cross-read rather than a source of upside. Note also that both series are equipment-unit series and ServiceTitan monetises job count and GTV, so the mapping is loose in both directions - which cuts against the finding as much as for it.

findings.finding: BLS PPI for 'Plastics Sewer, Stormdrain and Water Main Pipe' (WPU072106038) — CNM's single largest product exposure — averaged 185.2 across May/Jun/Jul 2026 (CNM's fiscal Q2, 4 May-2 Aug) versus 186.5 a year earlier, i.e. -0.7% y/y, against -8.2% y/y in CNM's fiscal Q1 (Feb-Apr 2026: 174.95 vs 190.48); the July 2026 reading of 188.565 is actually +1.9% ABOVE July 2025 and +8.2% above the March 2026 trough, so the deflation that drove the Sept-2025 guidance cut had fully reversed by the last month of this quarter.
findings.source_date: 2026-07-01 (latest monthly observation; series pulled 2026-09-08 via fredgraph.csv?id=WPU072106038)
findings.adversary_note: The arithmetic is right — I pulled WPU072106038 from FRED myself and every figure reconciles to the decimal (May/Jun/Jul 2026 = 182.669/184.350/188.565, mean 185.195 vs 186.492 a year earlier = -0.70%; Feb/Mar/Apr 2026 mean 174.951 vs 190.479 = -8.15%; Jul-26 188.565 vs Jul-25 185.009 = +1.92%; +8.24% off the Mar-26 trough of 174.202). The fiscal mapping is also right: CNM FQ1 FY26 = 2 Feb–3 May, FQ2 = 4 May–2 Aug, so Feb/Mar/Apr and May/Jun/Jul are correct. So this is not refutable on the data. It is, however, close to fully anticipated on the transmission, which is the part that matters. Three separate layers of publication: (1) the commodity move itself was mainstream trade press all year — pipe mills took ~10% in late March 2026 (Supply House Times / Plumbing & Mechanical April and July round-ups), US PVC contract prices ran +12–16% in Q2 2026 (ChemAnalyst, openPR tracker), Plastics Technology flagged PVC up in March; (2) the specific July datapoint that carries the +1.9% y/y was published by BLS on 2026-08-13, four weeks before this print; (3) decisively, management narrated exactly this shape on the 10 June Q1 call — Robyn Bradbury said 'we have started to see price increase announcements from our suppliers, but we haven't seen that hit our revenue numbers yet', 'we did do a little buying ahead of price increases on PVC... majority of that would hit in the third quarter', and 'PVC will still be down year-over-year even if we do get some uplift'. That last quote is the hunter's own -0.7% conclusion, pre-stated by the CFO. Gross margin was guided flat at the Q1 exit level of ~27.2% for the balance of the year and FY sales/EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed. What is genuinely NOT drawn out anywhere I can find: the sequential slope is steeper than 'modest' (+3.9% m/m in May alone, +8.2% in four months), and a distributor holding cheap inventory into a fast replacement-cost rise books a holding gain in the quarter the cost rises — that lands in FQ2 gross margin, not FQ3 revenue, and it is the one channel management's 'flat at 27.2%' guide does not obviously capture. Two things cut against sizing it large: PVC pipe is only ~15–20% of CNM revenue, and this PPI is a materially damped proxy for CNM's own realised pricing — CNM told the market in Sept 2025 that municipal PVC pipe was down ~15% y/y at a time WPU072106038 was down ~7.5%, roughly a 2x amplitude gap in the index's disfavour, so the index cannot be used to size the effect cleanly in either direction. I am not scoring this above 80 precisely because the fiscal-quarter re-cut plus the inventory-gain channel is a real residual; I am not scoring it below 60 because the company itself pre-announced the direction, the timing and the caveat.

findings.finding: Mueller Water Products — the largest US maker of fire hydrants and iron gate valves, sold almost entirely through waterworks distributors of which CNM is the biggest — reported its quarter ended 30 June 2026 (two of CNM's three Q2 months) on 5 August with net sales +4.1% to $395.9M driven 'primarily by higher pricing across most product lines' partially offset by slightly lower volumes, record adjusted EBITDA +24.3%, adjusted EPS +47.1%, and a third consecutive raise to FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance (to $367-372M).
findings.adversary_note: This is wire copy. Mueller Water Products released Q3 FY26 on GlobeNewswire on 2026-08-05 and it was covered same-day and next-day by Investing.com (twice, slides and transcript), StockTitan, MarketBeat, Motley Fool, Globe and Mail, Yahoo and AOL. Every number the hunter quotes — $395.9M net sales +4.1%, adjusted EBITDA $107.4M +24.3% with 440bp of margin expansion, adjusted EPS $0.50 +47.1%, FY26 EBITDA guidance raised to $367–372M — is in the press release verbatim, and I verified them against the 8-K exhibit. MWA is CNM's most-covered supplier and closest listed water-infrastructure comp; drawing the read-through is the single most routine thing an analyst covering this space does in the five weeks between the two prints. More importantly, the read-through is not the clean positive it is presented as. MWA's beat came from its own pricing actions plus tariff refunds plus cost management — MWA taking price across most product lines is an increase in CNM's cost of goods, not automatically an increase in CNM's margin, and it only helps CNM if pass-through leads the cost. And MWA reported 'slightly lower volumes', which is a mildly NEGATIVE volume read-through for CNM and sits alongside CNM#2 rather than against it. So the finding is both fully published and directionally contestable in the part that matters for CNM's EPS.

findings.finding: US single-family housing starts fell 9.9% m/m in July 2026 to an 808k SAAR, the lowest since November 2022 — a deterioration inside the final month of CNM's quarter and after management said on 10 June that residential lot development had 'largely stabilized' with 'no further deterioration'.
findings.adversary_note: This is a US Census Bureau macro release. Monthly New Residential Construction for July 2026 came out on 2026-08-18 and was covered by Census itself, HousingWire, TD Economics, Calculated Risk, Trading Economics, Red Book Lumber Data, the Housing Affordability Institute and mortgagenewsdaily — the hunter's own source is a 2026-08-21 recap of a release that was already three days old. I verified the numbers: single-family starts 808k SAAR, -9.9% m/m, total starts 1,239k, -12.4% m/m, permits +5.0%; the figures are right, only the 'lowest since November 2022' tag is not stated in the cited article. Beyond publication, this one is visibly in the price. CNM traded around $47 in early August, fell through the second half of the month, and set a new 52-week low in early September; WallStreetZen cut it to Hold on 2026-08-08 and Northcoast cut it from Buy to Neutral on 2026-08-26, eight days after the housing print. The options agree: 25-delta skew +3.24 vol points with the baseline calling the lean 'downside paid' and put/call open interest at 1.11. A bearish residential finding on a name at a 52-week low with puts bid is agreement with the market, not information. The mechanism also mostly misses the quarter being reported — residential lot development, which is what CNM actually sells into, LEADS starts, so a July starts print reaches this event through the forward guide rather than through the 2 August quarter-end. The only non-obvious sliver is the juxtaposition against management's 10 June 'stable relative to the fourth quarter and in line with our expectations' language, and that juxtaposition is an inference every sell-side preview will have run.

findings.finding: CNM raised $750M of 6.000% senior notes due 2034 on 1 July 2026 — inside fiscal Q2 — with proceeds earmarked for prepaying the 2028 term loan and for 'general corporate purposes, including... mergers and acquisitions, share repurchases', at the same time as it had $581M left on the $1bn authorisation, had just run its highest-ever quarterly buyback ($88M / 1.8M shares in Q1 plus $37M / 0.8M shares in the five weeks to 10 June), and management flagged 'a pretty notable uptick in the pipeline... to larger opportunities' and said it might 'overperform some of our M&A goals'.
findings.adversary_note: Every component of this is a separately published document, most of it wire copy, and the composite is a speculation rather than a fact. The notes were priced on 2026-06-25 (8-K pricing press release, plus same-week coverage by Yahoo Finance, Investing.com and TipRanks) and closed 1 July with the closing 8-K filed 2026-07-02, which I fetched and verified — $750M of 6.000% senior notes due 1 July 2034, use of proceeds exactly as quoted. But the same 8-K discloses that this sits alongside a new $800M senior term loan maturing 2033 replacing the 2028 term loan: TipRanks headlined it 'Core & Main refinances debt, extends maturities to 2033', which is the correct characterisation. A refinancing is not incremental M&A/buyback firepower, and the use-of-proceeds language listing 'organic growth, M&A, share repurchases and other initiatives' is boilerplate that appears in essentially every high-yield offering memorandum. The buyback figures ($88M/1.8M shares in Q1, $37M/0.8M in the five weeks to 10 June, $581M remaining on the $1bn authorisation) come from the Q1 10-Q and the 10 June call, public for three months, and the 'notable uptick in the pipeline... to larger opportunities' M&A quote is from that same call. What remains unpublished is only the inference that an unusually large Q2 buyback or a deal will land with tomorrow's print — and that is small even if right: $100M of repurchase against roughly $8.6bn of equity value is about 1% of shares and well under 1% of EPS, and the incremental interest cost of $750M at 6.000% (~$11M/quarter) is roughly a wash against the prepaid floating-rate term loan it replaced.

findings.finding: Sunbelt's buyback has been throttled by roughly 85%: treasury shares rose only from 3,993,501 (29 May 2026) to 4,699,397 (28 Aug 2026) — 705,896 shares in 13 weeks, ~54k/week or ~$4m/week at prevailing prices, an annualised ~$210m — versus $1,413m of buybacks in FY26 and 405,000 shares in the single week of 6-10 April 2026 under the same $1.5bn programme launched 2 March 2026; shares outstanding are flat at ~409.8m and the weekly notices show the pace decaying monotonically (405k Apr 6-10, 135k Apr 13-17, 75k Apr 27-May 1, 60k May 26-29, 60k Jun 15-18, 43k Jul 6-10, 17k Aug 10-14, 13k Aug 17-21, 23k Aug 24-28, 47k Aug 31-Sep 4).
findings.adversary_note: The two treasury endpoints check out exactly against the primary notices — 3,993,501 after the 26-29 May purchase and 4,699,397 after the 24-28 Aug purchase, a delta of 705,896 shares over 13 weeks, ~54k/week, and shares outstanding 409,803,623 — so the aggregation is not fabricated. But two of the three things the hunter builds on top of that arithmetic do not survive the primary record. First, 'decaying monotonically' is refuted by the hunter's own cited URL: detail/157 reports 47,000 shares for 31 Aug-4 Sep, after 17k, 13k and 23k, i.e. the pace has tripled off its trough in the last three weeks and the most recent week is at the 13-week average, not below it. Second, '~85%' is a peak-week-to-trough-week comparison dressed as a run-rate. On like-for-like verified endpoints the step-down is much smaller and it is a step, not a decay: 3,018,501 (2 Apr) → 3,708,501 (1 May) is 690,000 shares in ~4.2 weeks (164k/wk); 3,708,501 → 3,993,501 (29 May) is 285,000 (71k/wk); then 54k/wk for the next 13 weeks. So the whole break happens in the single week the company closed the $650m Reliant/Aries acquisition (1 May 2026) and it has been roughly flat since — May to August is -24%, not -85%. The 85% figure only exists against the FY26 total of $1,413m, which is not a run-rate: that number is dominated by the tail of the FIRST $1.5bn programme, an explicit 18-month completion sprint that ended 24 Feb 2026, and the company disclosed it as such on 23 June. Third, the cause is guided. On 23 June management disclosed the Reliant close, raised FY27 net rental capex to $2.05-2.45bn (an International Rental News headline that day was literally 'Sunbelt makes $650m acquisition and ups 2027 CapEx'), reported net leverage 1.6x, and ranked capital allocation as organic first, bolt-on M&A second, dividend and buyback last. A company that has just spent $650m of cash and raised capex buying back less is the disclosed plan executing, not a signal. On publication: each weekly notice is an RNS-format wire release syndicated same-day by TipRanks, Yahoo UK Finance, MarketScreener, Stockopedia and Reuters, with the treasury count and shares outstanding in the body — the inputs are ubiquitous. The hunter is right that nobody assembles them into a series (TipRanks' 1 Sep write-up of the same notice offers no pace commentary at all), which is what keeps this out of the 80s. On materiality: 54k shares/week against 6.1m ADV is under 0.2% of a single day's volume, so there is no flow-support channel; the foregone ~$1.2bn/yr of repurchase is ~4.3% of a $27.7bn cap in annual flow but only ~1.5-2% of shares per year, i.e. ~1-2% on out-year EPS, and it is spread over years rather than landing in tomorrow's print. The one live channel is the call — management said the Q1 quarterly dividend would be announced with Q1 results — but that cuts both ways: a dividend-for-buyback reallocation is the most likely reading and it is not bearish.

findings.finding: The Q1 FY27 (May-July 2026) volume setup is unusually well supported and the margin worry is pre-guided: the comp is +2.4% group rental revenue in Q1 FY26, Q4 FY26 exited at +8.0%, the $650m Reliant/Aries modular business closed 1 May 2026 so the full quarter is inorganically boosted, management flagged ~$70m of Q1-specific FIFA World Cup and UFC event revenue on the June call and said margins improve 'in the back half', and both peers reported record calendar Q2 and RAISED full-year guidance (URI rental revenue +12.7%, fleet productivity +3.4%, FY revenue guide lifted to $17.5-17.8bn from $16.9-17.4bn on 22 July; Herc rental revenue +23%, guidance raised on 28 July).
findings.adversary_note: Every component of this is in the wire copy, and most of it is in the company's own guidance. The Reliant/Aries $650m close on 1 May 2026 was announced in the 23 June Q4 press release and carried by Businesswire, Morningstar, Yahoo and the rental trade press the same morning; FY27 guidance of 5-8% rental revenue growth and $4.85-5.05bn adjusted EBITDA already contains it, so the 'inorganic boost' is definitionally in consensus rather than incremental to it. The ~$70m of FIFA World Cup and UFC event revenue was volunteered by management on the 23 June call and is in the transcript the hunter is citing — a number management itself labelled one-time, which is the opposite of an unpriced upside: sell-side has it in the Q1 bridge and will strip it out. 'Margins improve in the back half' is management's own words and is bearish for Q1 optics, not bullish; the market's reaction to that same guidance was -9.41% on the day. The peer data is the most-covered news in the sector this summer: United Rentals reported record Q2 and raised FY26 revenue guidance to $17.5-17.8bn from $16.9-17.4bn on 22 July, on rental revenue +12.7% and fleet productivity +3.4%, and Herc raised 2026 equipment rental revenue guidance to $4.375-4.475bn on Q2 revenue +20% — both were Reuters/Nasdaq/Globe and Mail headlines that repriced the whole group. The residual, genuinely-unpublished piece is only the inference: that the easy +2.4% Q1 FY26 comp plus a Q4 exit rate of +8.0% plus peer strength means Q1 volumes beat. But the options already express exactly that inference — negative 25d skew and a put/call OI ratio of 0.02 say the market is paying for upside into this print, not hedging it. A bullish finding on a name where the only thing anyone owns is calls is agreement, not information. The one honest deduction is that SUNB fell 14.35% over 20 days while the peers were raising, so the market has plainly declined to extrapolate — but the readier explanations for that gap are Sunbelt-specific margin scepticism (the same worry that produced the June drop, and the reason three analysts cut fair value to $78 from $83.64) and index flow around the FTSE exit and the 4 Sep S&P 500 rebalance that passed SUNB over.

findings.finding: Edge Retail Academy's US independent-jeweler panel shows the category decelerating sharply in August 2026 — gross sales +5% YoY (vs +18% in June and +10% in July), units -8%, average retail sale +14% — with the opening-price-point sterling silver / alternative metals category at -5% dollars and -19% units; August is month one of Signet's fiscal Q3 and the month the H2 guide has to be built on.
findings.adversary_note: The datapoint is published, on the hunter's own URL, five days before the print, in JCK — the jewelry industry's primary trade publication — and it is not a one-off leak but the September instalment of a monthly public series: Edge Retail Academy posts it on its own blog and JCK/InStore carried the June (+18%) and July (+10%) readings the same way, so the deceleration path the finding draws is itself a published series rather than a discovered one. Two further discounts. First, the macro narrative it embodies is exactly the stated cause of the 13.15% one-month drawdown already in the tape: Zacks/Yahoo and TipRanks catalyst pieces in the past month attribute SIG's slide to 'weak consumer demand and high gold prices squeezing profitability' and 'worries about a broader slowdown in middle-market jewelry buying' — which is verbatim the units-down / average-ticket-up shape of the Edge panel, and the World Gold Council's Q2 2026 release already put global jewellery volume at its lowest quarterly tonnage since the pandemic. Second, the panel is a poor proxy for Signet. Edge aggregates thousands of independent fine-jewelry stores, which skew natural-diamond bridal, custom and higher-ticket; Signet is mall and off-mall chain (Kay/Zales/Jared) plus Blue Nile/James Allen digital, is over 45% lab-grown in engagement rings, and has been running comps that diverge from the independent channel (Kay/Zales/Jared +6% comp in FY26 Q3). And August is fiscal Q3 month one — Signet's Q2 ended ~2026-08-01 — so it cannot touch a single reported number tomorrow. It reaches the print only through the Q3 comp guide, which is a real channel (UBS is publicly looking for low-single-digit positive Q3 comp guidance) but an indirect one. Against that, I concede what is genuinely undrawn: no equity-side coverage I could find connects the August Edge print to Signet's Q3 guide, and the stock did not move on 2026-09-03 (close 81.26 on 09-01, spot 82.06 on 09-08). That undrawn connection is why this is mid-scale and not 80.

findings.finding: The 15% Section 122 global import surcharge that underpinned Signet's 'mid-teens effective tariff rate for the year' expired 12:01am on 2026-07-24 and was replaced the same minute by Section 301 forced-labor duties of 10%–12.5% on the 60 economies covering Signet's sourcing base — a 2.5–5 point step down on India, the country Signet named as its principal tariff exposure, four days before its quarter ended and seven weeks after the FY27 guide was set.
findings.adversary_note: I refute this one on the facts before reaching the price. Two errors, and they invert the sign. (1) The Section 122 surcharge was 10% ad valorem, not 15%. The White House proclamation of 2026-02-20 says so in terms — 'I impose, for a period of 150 days, a temporary import surcharge of 10 percent ad valorem ... effective February 24, 2026' — and Gibson Dunn was still describing 'the current 10-percent-Section-122 tariffs' in its May 2026 CIT alert, while GHY's trade-compliance update (published 02-21, updated 02-24) states flatly that 'there have been no official communications supporting the 15% duty rate.' 15% is the statutory ceiling of Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974, not the rate imposed; Global Trade Alert is the only source I found modelling 15%, and it is an outlier against the proclamation text. (2) India's Section 301 forced-labor rate is 10%, per Honigman's own alert and per National Jeweler's trade coverage on 2026-07-24, which characterises the new 10–12.5% band against the prior across-the-board 10% as 'either maintenance or an increase.' So the transition for India is 10% to 10% — flat, not a 2.5–5 point step down. Across Signet's wider sourcing base it is worse than flat: China goes from 10%+25% to 12.5%+25%, and Thailand, Vietnam and the UAE all land in the 12.5% tier. There is no tariff tailwind here of the shape claimed. Separately, and independent of the arithmetic: the event is in the wire copy. Honigman, National Jeweler and Centurion Jewelry all covered it on or about 2026-07-24, 45 days before the print, and Centurion's piece is specifically headlined on jewelry-sourcing countries and notes Signet's heavy India sourcing; Simply Wall St has published Signet-specific tariff-exposure valuation notes quantifying the India dependence ('sources roughly half its merchandise from India'). Finally the mechanism barely reaches Q2 at all — 2026-07-24 leaves roughly one week inside a quarter that ended ~08-01, against months of inventory already landed, so it is a guide item only, and a guide raise on tariff relief is precisely what UBS published on 2026-09-08 (35–40 cents on the low end) and what the market is already looking for. The one real change the finding does not make — Section 301 exempts precious metals in raw and semi-manufactured form across all 60 economies — is also public in National Jeweler's 07-24 piece.

findings.finding: Signet has filed IEEPA refund claims on most goods where it was importer of record and had received only 'a small amount' as of 2026-06-02, with management stating it is too early to quantify the amount or timing 'as well as how any proceeds may be used' — meaning the FY27 guide contains none of it, while CBP had already built out mass electronic IEEPA refunds covering ~82% of affected entries by April 2026, i.e. during Signet's Q2.
findings.adversary_note: The fact is in the most public place a company fact can be: Signet's own Q1 FY27 earnings call on 2026-06-02, which is the hunter's own URL, and the accompanying 10-Q. Management volunteered it unprompted, and their exact words also cap the size and correct the finding: they are 'the importer of record on a small fraction of our purchases,' they have 'already submitted claims for most of those purchases,' and — contra the finding's 'the FY27 guide contains none of it' — the guidance explicitly includes a 'minimal tariff refund benefit.' So it is not excluded, it is included at a small number, and the reason it is small is structural: the bulk of Signet's merchandise arrives DDP through vendors, so those IEEPA refunds accrue to the vendors, not to Signet. Sizing it against Signet's own numbers: on roughly $3.0–3.5bn of annual merchandise purchases, a 'small fraction' as importer of record over the ~11 months IEEPA duties were collected, at a low-to-mid-teens effective rate, is order-of-magnitude $30–50m pre-tax plus statutory interest, on ~39.5m shares — real but a one-time, low-multiple item against $480–560m of adjusted operating income, and one the market will likely back out of adjusted EPS. The CBP scaffolding is accurate and public: the ~82% coverage figure comes from CBP's own status report to the CIT dated 2026-04-09 and was carried by Thompson Hine on 2026-04, and the CAPE launch on 2026-04-20 with 60–90 day turnaround was covered by NRF, RSM, Norton Rose Fulbright, UPS and National Jeweler — none of it Signet-specific. Simply Wall St has also published Signet-specific pieces on the tariff ruling reshaping its cost outlook. What I concede: I could find no analyst or press item that sizes Signet's refund, and none that draws the specific timing link — CBP mass-refunding through Signet's Q2, therefore a quantification or a P&L credit is plausible tomorrow. That undrawn timing link, plus the genuine possibility management uses the call to put a number on it for the first time, is what keeps this from 80. It is the one of the three that has a live, in-window channel to the print.

findings.finding: InnovAge's raised FY2026 guidance implies a Q4 adjusted EBITDA of only $14.7-19.7M (9M actual $70.3M = Q1 $17.6M + Q2 $22.2M + Q3 $30.495M, against a $85-90M full-year guide) and Q4 revenue of $222-247M versus Q3's $251.9M actual - i.e. a sequential revenue decline and a 4-5pp margin collapse - even though census rose to ~8,050, Colorado/state Medicaid rates are fixed through 30 June, Medicare risk scores are fixed for the calendar year, and the in-house pharmacy saving is structural; the identical structure in FY2025 (9M EBITDA $23.1M vs a $24-31M guide, implying Q4 of $0.9-7.9M) produced an actual Q4 of $11.3M and a full year of $34.5M, 11% above the top of guidance.
findings.adversary_note: The arithmetic is CORRECT — I checked every term against the primary releases. Q1 FY26 adj EBITDA $17.6M, Q2 $22.2M, Q3 $30.495M = $70.295M against a raised $85-90M guide, so implied Q4 is $14.7-19.7M; 9M revenue $236.1+$239.7+$251.943 = $727.7M against $950-975M, so implied Q4 revenue is $222.3-247.3M, a sequential decline from $251.9M and a 4.1-5.5pp margin step-down. The FY2025 analog is also exactly right: 9M FY25 adj EBITDA $23.1M against a reaffirmed $24-31M guide (implied Q4 $0.9-7.9M), actual Q4 $11.3M, FY $34.5M = 11.3% above the top. So no refutation on the sums. What kills most of the edge is that the Street has already done this subtraction and already assumes the beat: consensus Q4 FY26 revenue is $238.2-243.0M (above the $234.8M implied midpoint) and consensus EPS $0.07, with KeyBanc at $0.09 — on this company's ~$10M/qtr EBITDA-to-net-income bridge that puts consensus adj EBITDA at roughly $19.5M, i.e. AT the top of the implied guidance range, and KeyBanc above it. The 'guidance is sandbagged' observation is therefore embedded, not new. Worse for the mechanism, the identical setup exactly one year ago — the 2025-09-09 print, where Q4 FY25 came in at $11.3M versus an implied $0.9-7.9M and the full year landed 11% above the top of guidance — produced a reaction of only -2.81%, because the initial forward-year guide dominated. The baseline's own reaction history is the argument against this finding paying.

findings.finding: Colorado - InnovAge's home and largest state - enacted roughly $270M of Medicaid reimbursement cuts for FY2026-27, taking most fee-for-service rates down to 85% of Medicare from 2026-04-01 and layering a further 2.0% across-the-board reduction on HCBS waiver services for dates of service from 2026-07-01, published in the June 2026 provider bulletin after InnovAge last spoke to investors; PACE Medicaid capitation is set beneath an upper payment limit derived from exactly those FFS/HCBS costs, so the FY2027 Colorado rate InnovAge must build its first FY2027 guide around is flat-to-down rather than the mid-single-digit increases of prior years.
findings.adversary_note: The direction of this claim is management's own published guidance commentary from four months ago and it made a wire headline the same day: on the 2026-05-05 call the CFO said 'initial indications suggest rate increases in fiscal 2027 may be lower than what we have experienced historically', management flagged 'rate pressures emerge as we engage with our state Medicaid partners', and Seeking Alpha's news item was literally titled '...for fiscal 2026 amid early 2027 rate pressure signals'. The Colorado specifics are also public, and the largest of them is a year old, not new: the reset of most FFS rates to 85% of Medicare effective 2026-04-01 was published in HCPF's Special Provider Bulletin on rate reductions (B2500528) in September 2025 and was already in effect before the May call. The $270M and the 2% across-the-board cut effective 2026-07-01 came out of the Long Bill Polis signed on 2026-05-08 and were covered that week by CPR and roughly eight Colorado newspapers. So the finding's framing — 'published in the June 2026 provider bulletin after InnovAge last spoke to investors' — is right for the 2% HCBS piece and materially wrong for the 85%-of-Medicare piece, which is the bigger number. What I could NOT find published anywhere is the specific step the finding takes: PACE capitation set beneath a UPL derived from those same FFS/HCBS costs, therefore InnovAge's FY2027 Colorado rate flat-to-down. No sell-side note, no trade piece, and no company statement makes that link or sizes it, and HCPF's own FY2026-27 MSP budget request actually anticipates PACE expenditure GROWTH on enrollment, which cuts the other way. That unpublished linkage plus the fact that tonight is the first FY2027 guide is why this is not above 65.

findings.finding: TCO Group Holdings (Apax and Welsh Carson) registered 112,988,070 shares - 83.2% of the 135,736,393 outstanding - for resale on a Form S-3 filed 2026-07-31 and declared effective 2026-08-05, routed there via a confidential draft registration statement submitted 2026-07-17, with no 8-K and no press release at any point; the company then scheduled FY2026 results for 2026-09-08 after the close and a Wells Fargo Healthcare Conference presentation at 08:00 ET on 2026-09-09, which is the standard sequencing for a marketed block in the window immediately after the print, and the shelf removes the Rule 144 affiliate volume cap of roughly 1.36M shares per quarter that has been the only constraint on the sponsors selling.
findings.adversary_note: The registration is not obscure and it visibly moved the price. The S-3 hit EDGAR at 16:11 on Friday 2026-07-31; the stock fell 5.79% on Tuesday 2026-08-04, the second trading day after, and the effectiveness notice followed on 2026-08-05. It was written up by MarketScreener ('InnovAge Registers 113 Million Shares for Potential Resale by TCO Group Holdings'), StockTitan ('InnovAge holders register 113M shares for resale'), and twice by Simply Wall St, syndicated to Webull — all of which name TCO Group Holdings, the 112,988,070 shares, the 83.2% stake, the Apax and Welsh Carson vehicles, and explicitly the 'sizable potential secondary overhang'. So the finding's own framing that this happened 'with no 8-K and no press release at any point' is technically true of company disclosure and misleading about what the market saw. The Rule 144 arithmetic is right — 1% of 135,736,393 is 1.357M and beats the 878k average weekly volume test — and I do not dispute that removing the cap matters. What is genuinely unpublished is only the timing inference: that the print plus a Wells Fargo Healthcare Conference slot at 08:00 ET on 2026-09-09 is the sequencing for a marketed block. That is a plausible read but it is speculation stacked on a published fact, and the same schedule is the ordinary way a company times a fiscal-year print, so it does not carry the finding on its own. It also mostly resolves after the earnings reaction window rather than inside it.

findings.finding: Sell-side consensus for Q2 2026 is still $5.49m revenue (5 analysts, expecting +27.4% sequential growth) and -$0.16 EPS, six weeks after Nanox itself pre-announced Q2 revenue of 'approximately $4.0 to $4.1 million' -- a sequential decline; the headline on 2026-09-09 is therefore a mechanically guaranteed ~26% revenue miss.
findings.adversary_note: The substance is fully public and the tape already paid for it. Nanox pre-announced Q2 revenue of 'approximately $4.0 to $4.1 million' and the $31.4m 6/30 cash balance in a 6-K on 2026-07-23, and the same document introduced the going-concern language; the release was carried on StockTitan and MarketScreener the same day and the baseline records a -8.01% move on 2026-07-23. So the number that will print tomorrow has been known for seven weeks and cost the stock 8% on the day it became known. What survives is narrow and mechanical: two aggregators (FXEmpire $5.49m/5 analysts, MarketBeat via dailypolitical.com $5.376m on 2026-09-06) still carry a stale pre-announcement consensus, so wire copy tomorrow will read '~26% revenue miss'. I confirmed that stale consensus is itself published, which means the headline is foreseeable to anyone reading a preview — it is a print-day artefact on a $65m retail-heavy nano-cap, not new information about the company. I also checked the framing: $4.0-4.1m is a sequential decline (Q1 2026 revenue was $4,311k per the Q1 6-K exhibit) but a +33-37% y/y increase against $3.0m in Q2 2025, and the y/y framing is the one the company's own release will lead with. The claim is factually right and materially over-weighted.

findings.finding: Nanox has an unquantified 'comprehensive impairment assessment across all of its assets, including but not limited to long-lived assets and goodwill' still incomplete as of 2026-08-06, sitting against $57.364m of net intangibles and $30.551m of net PP&E at 2026-03-31 -- $88.0m of impairable carrying value versus a ~$68m market cap -- and it lands in the first quarter reported by a CFO who started 2026-08-01.
findings.adversary_note: The existence of the impairment review is published twice in primary filings and once on the wire, but the magnitude genuinely is not drawn out anywhere I could find. The 2026-07-23 6-K already said Nanox was evaluating 'impairment charges relating to certain long-lived assets and/or goodwill'; the 2026-08-06 6-K — which I fetched and which is primarily a registered direct offering of 8m units at $1.00 — broadens it to 'a comprehensive impairment assessment across all of its assets, including but not limited to long-lived assets and goodwill' with results that 'may differ, potentially materially'. That broadening sits inside an offering document and I found no article that picked it up. The carrying values are correct: I verified from the Q1 2026 6-K exhibit that intangible assets net are $57,364k and property and equipment net $30,551k at 2026-03-31 (goodwill is only $316k, so the hunter's $88.0m is right and its composition is intangibles plus PP&E, not goodwill). Against that, three things pull the number up. First, precedent: the company already took a $17.5m non-cash impairment on the Korean chip line in Q4 2025, reported 2026-04-20, so the market has seen this movie. Second, the arithmetic already argues the market has done the writedown itself — total shareholders' equity was $126.3m at 3/31 against a ~$65m market cap, i.e. the equity trades at roughly half book, and even a full $88m impairment leaves ~$38m of net assets, below where the shares are marked. A non-cash charge that only confirms a discount the tape already applies is not the same as new information. Third, it does not create a listing trigger: post-impairment equity of ~$38m still clears Nasdaq's $10m equity standard, and the sub-$1 bid price problem exists independently at $0.8676. What is left unpriced is the headline shock of a $100m+ GAAP net loss line landing in a first quarter signed off by a CFO who started 2026-08-01 (Guy Nathanzon, announced 2026-04-14) — a real kitchen-sink risk, but a second-order one.

findings.finding: The baseline's reaction history is wrong in a way that matters: the -44.01% on 2026-06-25 and -24.39% on 2026-04-20 were real earnings prints (Q1 2026 and FY2025), independently confirmed as a -43.99% post-release move, so this name's actual earnings base rate is 2-for-2 double-digit declines, not a 6.52% median.
findings.adversary_note: The factual identification is correct and I verified both dates independently — 2026-04-20 bmo was the Q4/FY2025 release and 2026-06-25 bmo was the Q1 2026 release, and NNOX closed 2026-06-25 at $0.8697, down ~44.6%, cross-checked against the stockanalysis.com history table where 2026-06-26 closes at $1.09 (+23.95%) off that base. So the baseline's -44.01% and -24.39% really are earnings reactions and the six-day cadence inference really is wrong. But that is a correction to our own priors, not information the market lacks: a two-observation reaction history is the tape, visible on every chart, and is as close to 100% public as anything in this brief. Worse, the base rate the claim wants to extract does not survive its own evidence. Both declines were caused by information arriving for the first time — the 2026-04-20 print introduced the $17.5m Korea impairment and a wider loss, and the 2026-06-25 print withdrew the $35m FY2026 revenue target and introduced substantial-doubt going-concern language. Every one of those four shocks has already been disclosed ahead of tomorrow, and revenue and cash have been pre-announced besides, so extrapolating '2-for-2 double-digit declines' onto a print whose contents are largely known is a category error rather than a base rate. The instability is visible too: the -44% was almost entirely retraced within two sessions (+23.95% then +11.01%). I am scoring this as near-fully priced on market-information grounds while noting it is nonetheless the most operationally useful of the four for the pipeline's own baseline hygiene.

findings.finding: Offsetting and pointing the other way: the four things that caused the last two collapses are all already disclosed -- 2026 guidance withdrawn, going-concern doubt introduced, Korea restructuring announced with a $17.5m charge taken, and Q2 revenue and the $31.4m 6/30 cash balance pre-announced -- while management has run a positive-news cadence into the print (Intel/OpenVINO 8/10, UK reseller 8/18, New England distributor 9/4) and needs a shareholder majority on 2026-09-17 to lift authorized capital by 50m shares.
findings.adversary_note: This finding is close to self-refuting as a novelty claim: its own thesis is that the four downside catalysts are already disclosed, and every single component I checked is a globenewswire press release or a filed 6-K, which is the definition of published. Guidance withdrawal and going-concern doubt: Q1 release, 2026-06-25. Korea restructuring and the $17.5m charge: Q4 2025 release, 2026-04-20, with the release itself stating total charges of ~$18.0m so only ~$0.5m remains. Q2 revenue and the $31.4m cash balance: 6-K, 2026-07-23. The positive-news cadence is three globenewswire items on 2026-08-10 (Intel Core Ultra / OpenVINO), 2026-08-18 (Vertec exclusive UK reseller for HealthOST) and 2026-09-04 (Associated X-Ray Imaging, New England) — all wire-distributed and all picked up by StockTitan. The 2026-09-17 meeting to lift authorised shares to 150m and grant CEO RSUs is in the proxy 6-K and has been written up by TipRanks and by StockTitan under the headline 'warns on cash runway before vote to boost share pool', so even the sceptical framing of the vote is on the wire. And the tape shows the cadence being paid for: the 5-day run-up is +7.51% into the print against -18.54% over 20 days, which is exactly the shape you would expect if the 9/4 distributor release was bid. The residual I will credit is the synthesis — that pre-announcing revenue, cash and going concern strips this print of the specific shocks that caused the last two collapses, leaving the impairment as the only live unknown — plus the incentive argument that management wants a clean tape two sessions before a majority vote it needs. That synthesis is an inference, not a fact, and I could not find it drawn out anywhere; it is why this is 79 rather than 92. Note it also directly cannibalises NNOX#0 and NNOX#2: if the de-risking argument holds, the revenue miss is stale and the two-print base rate is not transferable.

findings.finding: Meta's own Q2 2026 release (2026-07-29, 57 days after ODDITY last guided) shows average price per ad +12% y/y -- identical to Q1 2026 -- with ad impressions growth decelerating from +19% to +14%, i.e. the auction ODDITY blames for its CPA blow-up is still inflating at an unchanged rate while inventory growth slows; ODDITY's whole Q2/H2 case rests on its 'largest advertising partner' delivering an estimated 40-60% CPA recovery through system fixes.
findings.adversary_note: Every number in this claim comes from the single most-scrutinised earnings release on the tape. Meta's Q2 2026 press release (2026-07-29) states ad impressions +14% and average price per ad +12%; Meta's Q1 2026 release (2026-04-29) states +19% and +12%. Both are verified, both are public, and the specific observation that price-per-ad printed +12% for a second consecutive quarter has already been written up in ad-industry trade press (digitalapplied, 'Meta Ads After Q2: Planning for +12% Price Per Ad'). More important, the mechanism is misspecified. ODDITY's own 20-F and the June 2 call attribute the CPA blow-up to its largest partner down-weighting the 'Try Before You Buy' model because of high return rates -- an attribution/eligibility problem specific to ODDITY -- not to blended auction price inflation. Meta's +12% blended price per ad is roughly its normal run-rate and says almost nothing about whether TBYB traffic has been re-weighted. Meta-attributed orders are 'just under a quarter' of ODDITY revenue (ppc.land, from the company's own disclosure), so even a full read-across is a quarter-weight input. And ODDITY has already given the market a far more direct datum than Meta's blended pricing: on 2026-06-02 it disclosed IL MAKIAGE CPA down 28% sequentially in May, i.e. inside Meta's Q2 and after it. The residual novelty here is a framing of the consensus bear thesis that Jefferies, Goldman and KeyBanc have all published since February.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-03 a single line -- the October 16 2026 $7.50 put -- printed 24,001 contracts, 99.9% of the day's total ODD options volume and 2.8x the entire pre-existing open interest of 8,509, at a strike 48.4% below the then-spot of $14.54; on the same day the 3-month 90/110 skew FELL 4.76 percentage points to 0.73, which is the direction skew moves when size is sold to dealers, not bought.
findings.adversary_note: Every figure in this claim -- 24,001 contracts, 99.9% of the day's volume, 2.8x the 8,509 pre-existing open interest, the $14.54 spot, and the 90/110 three-month skew falling 4.76 points to 0.73 -- is stated verbatim in the investing.com article the hunter cites, published 2026-09-03, six days before the print. That is wire copy, and it is the definition of published. The one element that is the hunter's own is the inference that a falling skew alongside a 24k-lot put print means size was sold to dealers rather than bought, which the article explicitly declines to draw (it calls the flow 'defensive positioning' and 'tail-risk hedging'). On the merits, the hunter's inference is the better-supported one and I concede that much: if 24k deep-OTM puts had been bought, 90/110 skew would have risen, not fallen 4.76 points on the same session. But the tradeable content is very small. The premium involved is on the order of $0.5-1.0m against a $615m market cap, a $7.50 October strike 48% below spot is a lottery-ticket line whose print says nothing about the sign of a September 9 result, and the stock has already fallen 8.3% from the $14.54 quoted in the article to today's $13.33 -- so whatever information the flow carried has had five sessions to be absorbed.

findings.finding: The sealed baseline's eight-print history is wrong and only two of the eight 6-Ks are earnings: 2026-08-21 is the appointment of director David S. Cohen, 2026-07-30 is the AGM voting results, 2026-06-12/06-16 are the AGM proxy statement and proxy card, and 2026-03-12 is the $200m buyback authorisation -- leaving 2026-02-25 (-49.21%) and 2026-06-02 (-29.61%) as the only real earnings reactions, both of which are larger in absolute terms than the 20.7% currently implied.
findings.adversary_note: I checked all eight filings against EDGAR CIK 0001907085 and the headline conclusion is correct: only 2026-02-25 (FY2025 results, filed 07:06 UTC, exhibit 99-1) and 2026-06-02 (Q1 2026 results, 'issued a press release announcing financial results for the first quarter ended March 31, 2026') are earnings. But two of the enumerations are wrong. 2026-06-12 is NOT the AGM proxy statement -- it is the Oddity Finance exchangeable-note repurchase 6-K, the very document the other hunter builds ODD-b#2 on; the proxy statement and proxy card are 2026-06-16 (Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2, AGM of 2026-07-29). And 2026-01-12 is not addressed at all: it is the $350m credit-facility amendment 6-K. So the arithmetic 'two of eight' survives, but the working does not. On pricing: the facts themselves are about as public as facts get. ODD fell 49% on 2026-02-25 and ~30% on 2026-06-02; Calcalist, Reuters and every wire covered the February crash, Jefferies cut its target 72% from $64 to $18 that week, and the -79%-from-52-week-high in the baseline is the market's own record of it. The market does not need telling that ODD's last two earnings were catastrophic. What is genuinely new here is a correction to OUR sealed baseline file, not to the market's information set. The derived implication -- that a 20.74% implied move understates a 49%/30% history -- also rests on a three-day straddle with a 41.5% bid-ask on 945 contracts of open interest, so the 'only 20.7% is priced' half of the comparison is not a reliable statement of what the market pays, and two crisis prints where guidance collapsed from a standing start is not a base rate for a third print where guidance is already reset to -25/-30% and the stock is already down 79%.

findings.finding: ODDITY has pushed both 2026 interim reports roughly five weeks later than the prior year -- Q1 from 2025-04-29 to 2026-06-02 (+34 days) and Q2 from 2025-08-04 to 2026-09-09 (+36 days) -- while leaving the Q4/FY date untouched at February 25 in both 2025 and 2026, and has switched from after-close release with a next-morning call to a same-morning pre-open release.
findings.adversary_note: This is the one finding where I mostly concede the novelty and can only argue the mechanism. The dates check out against primary sources: Q1 2025 on 2025-04-29 and Q2 2025 on 2025-08-04 (both 6-Ks on EDGAR; the Q2 2025 advisory confirms 'after the market close on Monday, August 4' with the call the next morning), against Q1 2026 on 2026-06-02 and Q2 2026 on 2026-09-09 pre-open with a same-morning 08:30 ET call. That is +34 and +36 days, with FY unchanged at February 25 in both years, exactly as claimed. Each individual date is in a public press release, so nothing here is hidden -- but I could find no publication drawing the year-on-year delta, so this sits in the 'public but nobody has done the subtraction' band rather than lower. What I do dispute is the implication. ODDITY is an Israeli foreign private issuer: it has no SEC quarterly filing deadline at all, only the annual 20-F, so slipping interim dates is costless and carries none of the signalling a domestic issuer's 10-Q delay would. The FY date being untouched is consistent with that -- the only deadline-bound report did not move. And the direction is ambiguous even if the delay is deliberate: reporting Q2 seventy days after quarter end means management has two extra months of Q3 CPA data when it guides, which is as likely to enable a credible recovery narrative as to conceal a bad one.

findings.finding: IL MAKIAGE's own web traffic -- whose single largest channel is Display advertising at 28.84% of desktop visits, i.e. a direct read on the paid-acquisition funnel management says it is re-scaling -- kept falling sequentially all summer: 2.44M visits in June 2026, 2.36M in July (-3.18%), ~2.3M in August (-4.73%), with the site's global rank sliding from ~10,747 to ~15,447 over three months.
findings.source_date: 2026-09-08 (page states: 'In July ilmakiage.com received 2.36M visits', down 3.18% from June's 2.44M)
findings.adversary_note: The series is free, public and on the exact URL cited, and alt-data desks have watched ilmakiage.com since the February crash -- but the numbers as reported do not reconcile, and the evidentiary weight is low even where they do. Fetching the cited Semrush page today returns May 2.51M, June 2.44M, July 2.36M visits and a global rank of 23,439 -- not the 10,747-to-15,447 slide the finding reports. The 15,447 figure appears on Similarweb attached to an April 2026 page, so the rank series here is conflated across two providers and at least one wrong month. There is no August figure on the cited Semrush page at all; the '~2.3M in August (-4.73%)' is the hunter's extrapolation presented alongside measured months. And the 28.84% Display share of desktop visits is behind Semrush's paywall -- the free page shows Direct 42.18% and Google 14.1% and no channel split -- so the load-bearing premise that this is 'a direct read on the paid-acquisition funnel' is not verifiable from the source given. On weight: Semrush and Similarweb are panel-modelled, not measured, and month-over-month deltas of 3-5% on a 2.4M-visit site are inside both the model error and ordinary summer seasonality for colour cosmetics. Most damaging of all, the sign may be backwards. The company has already guided Q2 revenue down 25-30% year on year. A site drifting down 3% a month sequentially is not evidence that guide is being missed; if anything it is consistent with, or better than, a guide of that severity.

findings.finding: Short interest is 6.58M shares, ~23% of a 28.1M share float with 6-9 days to cover, and it ROSE from ~6.00M a month earlier -- shorts added into the rally and into the print; the most parsimonious reading of the baseline's -16.19 vol-point 25-delta skew is a crowded short book buying OTM calls as gap protection, not the market making a bullish statement.
findings.source_date: 2026-09-08 (page shows short interest 6.58M, 23.04% of float, short ratio 8.96, dated September 8, 2026, 'increased from 6.00 million shares the previous month')
findings.adversary_note: The share count is right and I verified it independently on two sites, which is precisely the problem: 6,583,805 shares short against 5,998,488 the prior settlement is published on stockanalysis.com, MarketBeat, Fintel, Nasdaq and Benzinga, and it is the FINRA 2026-08-14 settlement, disseminated around 2026-08-26. Twelve days before the print, on every free retail terminal, is not information. Two qualifications. First, the '23% of float' is denominator-dependent: stockanalysis reaches it on a 28.57M Class A float, MarketBeat publishes 11.43% on a wider base for the identical share count. The borrow-relevant number is arguably the Class A one, but the headline percentage is contestable rather than a fact. Second, 'shorts added into the rally and into the print' over-reads a series that stops on 2026-08-14: it says nothing about the last three and a half weeks, during which the stock has fallen 7.4% in five sessions. Third and most important, the skew reinterpretation is refuted by the other hunter's evidence on the same tape. The claim is that the -16.19 vol-point skew is a crowded short book buying OTM calls as gap protection. On 2026-09-03, the day the skew inverted, ODD traded 24,012 puts against four calls. There was no call buying. The mechanical cause of calls being bid relative to puts was put-side supply, not call-side demand -- and independently, with total front-expiry open interest of 945 contracts and an ATM bid-ask of 41.5% of mid, that skew reading is not measurable enough to sustain either story.

findings.finding: A 6-K filed 2026-06-12 discloses that on 2026-06-11 Oddity Finance LLC privately agreed to repurchase $50M face of its 0% Exchangeable Senior Notes due 2030 for $35M cash, closing 2026-06-17 and leaving $550M outstanding -- roughly a $15M pre-tax gain on extinguishment that lands in Q2 GAAP results and is not in the $0.1223 adjusted consensus, and it prices the company's own paper at ~70 cents in June.
findings.adversary_note: The transaction is correctly described -- I read the 6-K and it says $50m face of the 0% Exchangeable Senior Notes due 2030 repurchased for $35m, closing 2026-06-17, $550m remaining -- and it does land inside Q2. It is also correctly noted that a gain on extinguishment sits in GAAP and not in the $0.1223 adjusted consensus, so it cannot mechanically produce an adjusted beat. But this was filed on EDGAR on 2026-06-12 and picked up the same day by TipRanks, GuruFocus and StockTitan, and ODD closed +6.93% that session. That is publication plus a visible tape reaction on the day the information arrived, which is the strongest form of 'priced'. What remains unpublished is only the arithmetic step -- roughly $14-15m pre-tax gain, given ASU 2020-06 leaves the notes carried near face less unamortised issuance cost -- and that step is mechanical enough that any analyst carrying a GAAP line already has it. The credit inference is the weaker half. A 0% coupon note due 2030 whose conversion option is worthless with the stock down 79% is a pure-discount instrument; 70 cents over roughly four years is a ~9% yield, which is high-yield pricing, not distress, and most of the discount is arithmetic rather than credit. The company drew $350m of amended facilities in January and has been buying back stock under a $200m authorisation. The realistic effect on 2026-09-09 is a possible headline-versus-adjusted EPS confusion in the first minutes of the tape.

findings.finding: The US$10m buyback that drove the stock +21.5% on 2026-09-03 and anchored the +76% five-session run is 17 Education's sixth consecutive annual US$10m authorisation (Nov 2021, Sep 2022, Sep 2023, Sep 2024, Sep 2025, Sep 2026) and is a straight rollover of the identical US$10m program that ran 2025-09-04 to 2026-09-04 and expired four days before this one started.
findings.adversary_note: Every input to this claim is on the public wire and has been for years: the Nov-2021 authorisation is a GlobeNewswire release, the Sep-2022 (effective Nov 2 2022) and Sep-2023 (effective Nov 2 2023) authorisations are filed 6-Ks, and the FY2025 20-F filed 2026-04-29 states in terms that 'on September 3, 2025 the board authorized up to US$10,000 thousand ... over the 12 months starting from September 4, 2025.' The 2026-09-03 release itself is wire copy carried by GlobeNewswire, Nasdaq, Manila Times and StockTitan. So the rollover is assemblable by anyone who opens the last five annual releases. What is not published anywhere I can find is the word 'rollover' — no article, no note, no aggregator drew the line, and the market paid +21.49% on 2,789,500 ADSs (median 20d before: 4,600) for a headline it evidently read as new capital return. That tape is affirmative evidence the conclusion is NOT in the price, which is why this does not sit above 50. Two corrections, though. First, the claim is factually wrong on its own detail: per the FY2025 20-F the prior programme ran 12 months from 2026-09-04's predecessor date of September 4, 2025 — i.e. to 2026-09-04, which is one day AFTER the new programme began on 2026-09-03. There was no four-day gap; there was a one-day overlap. The substantive point survives and is arguably strengthened, but the stated fact is wrong. Second, the mechanism only reaches tonight's print indirectly: the buyback is not in the Q2 release, so this only pays if a soft print becomes the trigger for unwinding a 74% five-day run built on it.

findings.finding: Q1 2026's headline RMB99.5m revenue (+359% YoY) was drawn largely out of a one-off pre-sale balance rather than new demand: deferred revenue and advances from customers fell from RMB165.9m at 2025-12-31 to RMB104.5m at 2026-03-31, a RMB61.5m drawdown equal to 62% of the quarter's revenue, and cash plus term deposits fell RMB54.6m (RMB406.9m to RMB352.3m) against a reported net loss of only RMB19.4m - 2.8x the loss.
findings.adversary_note: Every figure checks out exactly against the primary source: the Q1 2026 6-K exhibit shows net revenues RMB99.5m (+359.0%), net loss RMB19.4m, deferred revenue and advances RMB165.9m at 2025-12-31 falling to RMB104.5m at 2026-03-31, and cash+restricted+term deposits RMB407.0m falling to RMB352.4m. So the data is public, it has been public since 2026-06-16, and the market saw it: the stock fell 4.58% that day. That is the case for pricing. The case against is stronger. The datum sits as two unremarked line items on the face of a balance sheet inside a 6-K exhibit; every piece of coverage I can find — GlobeNewswire, StockTitan, GuruFocus, Investing.com's transcript writeup, Simply Wall St — leads on '+359% revenue', 'gross margin 61.9% from 36.2%' and 'loss narrowed 37%', and none of them mentions deferred revenue. Management did not mention deferred revenue, pre-sales, billings or cash burn anywhere on the Q1 call. So the fact is published in an obscure place with its implication drawn nowhere, which is the 20-40 band. Two things hold it off a lower number. The interpretation is contested: prior-year seasonality was a drawdown too (RMB40.4m at 2024-12-31 to RMB36.9m at 2025-03-31, per the Q1 2025 release), so Q1 draws down as a rule — this one is just far bigger. And the sign is not one-way: implied new billings of ~RMB38m against ~RMB18m a year earlier is still more than a doubling, and RMB104.5m of remaining deferred revenue is 2.8x the year-ago balance. 'Drawn largely out of a one-off pre-sale balance rather than new demand' overstates what the numbers show. The cash leg is the harder half: RMB54.6m of cash out against a RMB19.4m accounting loss is real and it is 2.8x, on a company whose entire market capitalisation (~10.84m ADS at 1 ADS : 50 shares, times spot) is below its own cash balance.

findings.finding: The company dismissed Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu as its auditor effective 2026-05-27 and appointed Marcum Asia CPAs LLP for the year ending 2026-12-31 - i.e. it dropped a Big Four auditor two quarters after its revenue recognition profile changed beyond recognition, and the Q2 2026 numbers about to be released are the first reported under the new firm.
findings.adversary_note: This is in aggregator wire copy and it moved the stock on the day it became known. TipRanks ran 'Replaces Deloitte With Marcum Asia as Auditor' and StockTitan ran 'Auditor switch at 17 Education (NASDAQ: YQ) from Deloitte to Marcum Asia', both off the 6-K of 2026-05-28, and the stock fell 3.99% that session. A Big Four to small-cap-China-specialist auditor switch at a Chinese ADR is one of the most reflexively flagged governance events there is; it is not obscure and it is not undrawn. Beyond the pricing question, the mechanism to tonight barely exists. The claim's own hook — 'the Q2 2026 numbers about to be released are the first reported under the new firm' — is close to vacuous: these are unaudited quarterly results from a foreign private issuer, Marcum Asia is engaged for the year ending 2026-12-31, and no auditor signs or is named in a 6-K quarterly release. The engagement bites at the FY2026 audit in spring 2027, not tonight. The one thing the claim adds that the wire copy did not is the juxtaposition with the Q1 revenue-recognition inflection, and I will credit that as the reason this is 75 and not 90 — but the 6-K also states plainly that there were no disagreements, no reportable events, and no qualified or modified opinions in 2024 or 2025, which is the disclosure that lets the market file this and move on, and it evidently did.

findings.finding: Deferred revenue and advances from customers fell from RMB165.9m at 31-Dec-2025 to RMB104.5m at 31-Mar-2026, so RMB61.4m of the RMB99.5m of Q1 revenue that produced the headline '+359% YoY' was a drawdown of Q4 2025 pre-sale orders: implied new billings were only about RMB38m, less than the RMB43.2m spent on sales and marketing in the same quarter, and cash plus restricted cash plus term deposits fell RMB54.6m (RMB407.0m to RMB352.4m) against a reported net loss of just RMB19.4m.
findings.adversary_note: This is the same document and substantially the same arithmetic as YQ-a#1, so it inherits the same publication status: the numbers are exact against the 6-K exhibit of 2026-06-17, the market saw that release and fell 4.58%, and no piece of coverage anywhere draws out the deferred revenue line. It is scored a shade higher than a#1 because the extra step it takes is the weaker one. 'Implied new billings of about RMB38m, less than the RMB43.2m spent on sales and marketing' is a rhetorical benchmark, not a threshold that means anything: billings-below-S&M is the normal condition of a consumer product in year one of national launch, and the same computation for Q1 2025 gives implied billings of ~RMB18m against S&M of RMB13m, so the comparison has moved in the company's favour on a growth basis even as it fails the absolute test. The 'so RMB61.4m of the RMB99.5m was a drawdown of Q4 2025 pre-sale orders' framing also assumes the deferred balance runs off one-for-one into revenue with no new deferral inside the quarter, which the disclosure does not support — RMB104.5m of deferred revenue remained, 2.8x the year-ago RMB36.9m. The cash leg is the part I cannot argue with: RMB54.6m out against a RMB19.4m book loss, on a balance sheet whose US$51.1m of cash exceeds the company's entire market capitalisation at ~10.84m ADS-equivalent. That is material, it is unremarked, and tonight's Q2 balance sheet resolves it directly.

findings.finding: The US$10 million buyback authorisation announced 2026-09-03 that triggered the +21.5% jump is at least the fourth identical US$10 million 12-month authorisation the company has issued (November 2021, September 2024, September 2025, September 2026), and the FY2024 20-F discloses that only approximately US$0.1 million had actually been repurchased under the September 2024 programme as of 31-Dec-2024 — about 1% of the authorisation.
findings.adversary_note: The authorisation itself is wire copy from 2026-09-03 and the prior authorisations are filed 6-Ks and press releases, so the 'fourth identical US$10m programme' half is assemblable from public documents and is the weaker version of what YQ-a#0 says. The execution statistic is the genuinely undrawn part — I could not find any article, note or aggregator that states how little has actually been repurchased — but I can partly refute the framing from the same class of document the claim cites. The FY2025 20-F, filed 2026-04-29, discloses repurchases of 105,636,192 Class A shares (2,112,724 ADSs) for RMB51,393 thousand in FY2023 — roughly US$7.2m, i.e. most of a full US$10m programme actually executed. FY2024 was RMB1,070 thousand (~US$0.15m) and FY2025 was RMB3,516 thousand (~US$0.5m). So 'about 1% of the authorisation' is true of the single worst year and is not the company's record; the honest recent number is ~5% of the last programme, and the honest full record includes one programme executed at ~70%. That said, the directional point survives and it matters more here than it would elsewhere: US$10m against a market capitalisation of roughly US$40m is 25% of the company, so if the market is capitalising the authorisation at anything like face value it is capitalising something the issuer spent US$0.5m on over the preceding twelve months. That gap is real and undrawn, which is why this is not above 50.

findings.finding: The CEO's near-daily Form 4 open-market ADS purchases through August and early September — reported by aggregators as conviction buying — are executions of a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan entered into on 2026-03-31 with Tiger Brokers (NZ) Limited covering 30-Jun-2026 to 31-Mar-2028, a fact disclosed for the first time in Item 6 of a Schedule 13D/A filed on the morning of the print itself.
findings.adversary_note: I checked this against the primary sources and the core factual claim holds up better than most things I judged today. Two of the Form 4s covering the July and August purchases (accessions 0001193125-26-308294 and 0001193125-26-361706) carry aff10b5One = false and no footnote referencing any trading plan, and StockTitan's own summary of the 2026-09-03 Form 4 reads 'CEO purchased 10,284 ADSs without preset plan'. Meanwhile TipRanks ran the conviction framing outright: 'CEO's Bold Move Signals Growing Confidence in EdTech Leader'. So the narrative the claim is attacking is real and published, and the correction genuinely first appears in today's 13D/A. Three things keep this from being a low number. First, the 13D/A is public and an aggregator has already summarised it before the close — StockTitan's YQ overview carries a 2026-09-08 item headed 'An insider stock-buying plan at 17 Education (YQ) runs into 2028'. It is hours old and obscure, but it is out, and the stock is up ~4% today with it out. Second, the claim mislocates it: the plan is disclosed in Item 3 of the 13D/A, not Item 6, and Item 6 in fact says there are no other contracts or arrangements. Third and most important, the size does not support the rhetoric. The 13D/A states Future Glory bought 110,628 ADSs (5,531,400 Class A shares) for approximately US$0.24 million between 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-03. Debunking a US$240,000 signal on a company with roughly US$40m of market capitalisation is a sentiment correction, not a numbers event, and it does not touch tonight's P&L at all.

findings.finding: Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu was dismissed as auditor effective 2026-05-27 — four weeks after signing the FY2025 20-F and three weeks before the Q1 revenue inflection was reported — and replaced by Marcum Asia CPAs LLP, a firm the PCAOB censured and fined US$100,000 on 2025-09-23.
findings.adversary_note: Both halves of this are separately published and one of them moved the stock on the day. The auditor switch was carried by TipRanks and StockTitan on 2026-05-28 and the shares fell 3.99% that session. The Marcum Asia sanction is a PCAOB press release of 2025-09-23 and was covered by Accounting Today, CPA Practice Advisor and International Accounting Bulletin the following day; the numbers in the claim — censure, US$100,000 civil penalty — are exactly right. So there is no unpublished fact here, only an unpublished juxtaposition, and I score it marginally below the sibling YQ-a#2 only because the PCAOB detail has never been attached to YQ specifically. The juxtaposition is also weaker than it reads. The PCAOB order concerns MarcumBP's transfer of draft workpapers to a successor auditor on Gridsum Holding — a predecessor/successor communications failure on an unrelated issuer, penalised at US$100,000, not an audit-quality finding on a China client's revenue recognition. And the timing hook cuts both ways: the 6-K states there were no disagreements, no reportable events, and no qualified or modified opinions from Deloitte for 2024 or 2025, which is precisely the disclosure that lets a market file an auditor switch and move on. The dates check out — 20-F filed 2026-04-29, dismissal effective 2026-05-27, four weeks — but a four-week gap after a clean 20-F sign-off is also the ordinary time at which an issuer switches auditors, because that is when the prior engagement ends.

findings.finding: There is a real structural bid under the stock that cuts against the fade: the CEO's 10b5-1 plan runs to 31-Mar-2028 and the US$10m authorisation is live, against a non-Liu share base of only about 6.4m ADS-equivalent (542.2m shares outstanding less Andy Chang Liu's 223.9m / 41.30%) and a pre-spike median volume of 4,600 ADSs a day.
findings.adversary_note: This is the highest number I am giving and it is the one I am most confident in, for three separate reasons. First, it has already been published in exactly this framing on the day of the print: StockTitan's YQ overview carries a 2026-09-08 item headed 'An insider stock-buying plan at 17 Education (YQ) runs into 2028' — the bullish read of the 13D/A is not a discovery, it is today's aggregator headline. Second, the tiny non-insider base is the single most structural and most visible fact about this security. The arithmetic is right (542.2m less 223.9m is 318.3m Class A-equivalent, and at the 1 ADS : 50 ratio effective December 2023 that is 6.37m ADSs) but a small float is not news, it is the permanent condition of the name, and the squeeze it enables is not pending — it has already happened. The stock traded 2,789,500 ADSs on 2026-09-03, roughly 44% of the entire non-Liu base in one session, ran +74.5% in five sessions, and average 20-day volume now stands at 157,802 against the 4,600 the claim cites as the pre-spike median. Citing the 4,600 as if it still described the market is citing a number the run-up already destroyed. Third, the two legs of the 'structural bid' do not survive sizing. The 10b5-1 plan bought 110,628 ADSs for approximately US$0.24 million over nine weeks — about US$27,000 a week — against current dollar volume of several hundred thousand a day; that is not a bid, it is a rounding error, and the 13D/A explicitly says the plan is subject to price restrictions and volume limitations while every disclosed execution fell between roughly US$1.89 and US$2.46, well below the current US$3.96. There is no evidence in the document that the plan buys anything at all up here, which would invert the claim outright. The US$10m authorisation leg is refuted by the hunters' own other finding: the FY2025 20-F shows US$0.5m actually repurchased over the last twelve months, so a live authorisation is not a live bid.
